newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Grains - S.Koreans tendering for wheat/meal.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grains - S.Koreans tendering for wheat/meal.

text.p: South Korean grain importers are seen taking a high profile this week as its biggest buyer re-tenders for feed wheat and meal after passing on the purchases last week, traders said on Monday.

The National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) had passed on tenders last Tuesday for 52,000 tonnes of feed wheat, 30,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellets and 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal due to higher-than-expected prices, they said.
The NLCF is expected to invite tenders again this week in a move which may spur more purchases by other Korean buyers.
"The NLCF purchase is expected to ignite other local buyers' interest in feed wheat, especially Canadian feed wheat," a trader with a foreign grain trading company in Korea said.
"Other buyers will jump into the market if feed prices fall just below the level of current corn prices," the trader said.
Several traders said, however, that other buyers may replace some of their feed wheat requirements with corn for early shipment due to high feed wheat prices.
They said the current feed wheat price for August shipment was quoted at about US$140 a tonne C&F, slightly higher than corn prices of $138 a tonne C&F.
Last week, South Korean corn buyers had bought an additional 117,500 tonnes of corn through closed tenders for shipment between August and September, traders said.
The Korea Feed Association last Thursday bought 52,500 tonnes of optional origin corn at between $128.69-$133.69 a tonne C&F from Tomen for arrival by September 15 to the western port of Inchon.
The KFA also bought 12,500 tonnes of Chinese corn from Toepfer at $132.50 a tonne C&F for arrival around the same date.
Another group known as the Top Margin Committee bought 52,500 tonnes of optional origin corn at between $133.95-$134.75 a tonne C&F from Cargill for October 15 arrival, dealers said.
The Korea Flour Milling Corp was also expected to re-invite tenders for 16,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat this week for July 5 to August shipment after passing last Thursday due to high prices.
In Japan, importers finished covering more than 90 percent of their U.S. corn requirements for the third quarter of 1997 and will probably be sidelined this week, traders said.
"We've covered 90 to 95 percent of U.S. corn requirement for the third quarter, and will buy the rest gradually," a corn dealer at a Tokyo-based trade house said.
Japan's corn premiums for the fourth quarter of this year were seen at between 96-97 U.S. cents a bushel over CBOT September futures.
Traders said they will wait for premiums to ease to below 95 U.S. cents before launching buying for the fourth quarter.
"Until the premiums fall to that level, we'll be sidelined," a dealer at a trading house in Japan said.

Last week an advisory body to the agricultural ministry endorsed a plan to reduce prices for Japan's small domestic wheat crop which will come down for the first time in six years, the Kyodo new agency reported.
The Rice Price Council agreed cut its purchase price for wheat, barley and rye harvested this year by 0.95 percent.
The price at which the government buys wheat from growers will drop to 9,023 yen per 60 kgs from 9,110 yen last year.

For barley, prices will be cut to 6,478 yen from 6,540 yen per 50 kg last year and to 9,331 yen from 9,421 yen per 60 kg for rye. The government is aiming to reduce the purchase prices to narrow the wide price gap between domestically produced wheat and imports.

In the shipping market, an official with Pan Ocean Shipping Co Ltd in South Korea said freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were flat at $12 a tonne over the past week for nearby shipments of Panamax-sized cargoes.
Rates from the U.S. Gulf for nearby shipments of Panamax-sized cargoes were unchanged at $20.50 a tonne.
